$$

$$

$$

Then, we apply the power rule of exponents. This gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}{5}^{2(n-10)}={5}^{4(n+4)}\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}2(n-10) & =4(n+4) \\ 2n-20 & =4n+16 \\ -2n & =36 \\ n & =-18\end{aligned}

$$

$$

Then, we apply the power rule and the product rule of exponents. This gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}{2}^{2x}\cdot {2}^{4(3x+3)} & ={2}^{6} \\ {2}^{2x+4(3x+3)} & ={2}^{6}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since both sides of the equation share the same base $(2)$, we equate the exponents and solve for $x:$

$$
